payload.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

ambiguities: It is not stated over which coefficient ring the polynomial is taken, although the intended meaning is usually a polynomial with integer coefficients.
The statement does not specify whether the polynomial is required to be nonzero, though the ratio of q-binomial coefficients is expected to be nonzero when defined.
The notation uses l as a variable name, which may be visually confused with the digit 1.
implicit_assumptions_surfaced: The phrase polynomial in q means the quotient is a genuine polynomial after cancellation, not just a rational function.
Nonnegative coefficients means every coefficient is at least zero.
The statement treats q as an indeterminate rather than a number.
The q-binomial coefficient is assumed to be the standard Gaussian binomial coefficient.

domain_restrictions: k and l are between 0 and n inclusive
the q-binomial coefficients are taken in the standard Gaussian sense
the ratio is only considered under the condition that it simplifies to a polynomial in q
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer triple n, k, l with 0 <= k <= n and 0 <= l <= n, if the quotient of the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient indexed by k and the one indexed by l is actually a polynomial in q, then every coefficient of that polynomial is nonnegative.
quantifier_order: for all integers n, k, l
assume 0 <= k <= n and 0 <= l <= n
if the ratio of the two q-binomial coefficients is a polynomial in q
then that polynomial has only nonnegative coefficients

variables.name: k
variables.role: lower index of the first q-binomial coefficient

variables.name: l
variables.role: lower index of the second q-binomial coefficient

variables.name: q
variables.role: parameter of the q-binomial coefficient and the ratio

witness_dependencies: The conclusion depends on the given integers n, k, l and on the assumption that the ratio is polynomial in q
